Suggested 60-minute split:
- B, dogwhistle/heldout.py, 40 min. This is the primary file. Confirm the return order and the naming, and check callers and tests that use the paths.
- A, dogwhistle/study.py, 15 min. It is a near-miss that uses the `study/` folder, not `followup/`. `run_paths` (line 182) returns the sender seal and a single digest path. `public_ledger_digest_path` (line 187) returns only the ledger digest path. Neither returns both digest paths under `followup/`.
- C, dogwhistle/visibility.py, and D, dogwhistle/honest.py, 5 min together. Each has only a single `seal_path` helper, so a quick skim to rule them out is enough.

The four handoff_refs files all contain the same generic text, so they gave no file-specific priority. I based the choice of refs on the repo code. I chose B and A, the same two refs as the incoming handoff. I did not run tests.
